arguments.root_cause_statement: The Service shop/catalog selects pods with the label app=catalog-api, but the Deployment shop/catalog stamps its pods with app=catalog (.spec.template.metadata.labels). No pod in the namespace carries app=catalog-api, so the endpoint controller writes an Endpoints object for the Service with no addresses at all. The catalog Deployment itself is healthy (2/2 Ready, no restarts), which is why the deployment reports all replicas Ready while traffic sent to the Service ClusterIP has nowhere to land; the storefront gateway's polls of the catalog Service log repeated "catalog fetch FAILED (timeout or connection refused)". Fixing the Service selector to app=catalog restores endpoints.
arguments.mechanism: The Service shop/catalog has .spec.selector set to {app: catalog-api}, while the pods that back the catalog workload carry the label app=catalog, so nothing in the namespace matches the selector and the endpoint controller populates the Service's Endpoints object with zero addresses; connections to the Service ClusterIP:8080 therefore have no backend to be routed to and fail.

evidence.claim: The paged Service has no endpoint addresses even though the catalog Deployment is fully Ready.
The storefront gateway's calls to the catalog Service never complete.
evidence.quote: gateway: catalog fetch FAILED (timeout or connection refused)

evidence.claim: The Service selector names a label value no pod carries.
The catalog Deployment labels its pods app=catalog, not app=catalog-api.
The endpoint controller produced an Endpoints object for catalog with no subsets/addresses.
Both catalog pods are Running and Ready with no restarts, so readiness is not what removed them from the Endpoints.
evidence.quote: pod/catalog-65498fccb-g52gl phase=Running labels={app=catalog, pod-template-hash=65498fccb} node=incident-lab-control-plane api(ready=True,restarts=0)

ruled_out.alternative: The catalog pods are unhealthy or failing their readiness probe, so they were dropped from the Endpoints.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Both catalog pods are Running with ready=True and zero restarts, and the Deployment reports 2/2 ready.

ruled_out.alternative: The Service port or targetPort is misconfigured so traffic reaches the pods on the wrong port.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The Service listens on 8080 with targetPort 8080, which matches the container's named http port 8080 in the Deployment template; the port mapping is consistent.

ruled_out.alternative: The storefront-gateway Deployment itself is broken or crash-looping.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The gateway pod is Running and Ready with no restarts and is actively polling; it only reports failures against the catalog backend.
ruled_out.quote: pod/storefront-gateway-6785fd7b5d-cq9bt phase=Running labels={app=storefront-gateway, pod-template-hash=6785fd7b5d} node=incident-lab-control-plane gateway(ready=True,restarts=0)

verification.command: kubectl -n shop get service catalog -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'
kubectl -n shop get endpoints catalog -o yaml
